contexts.text: Terah was a nation named from Terah as its father, by which nation is signified idolatrous worship. AC 1355. AC 1356, Explained. AC 1359.
Here it is very plain that Terah, Abram, and Nahor were idolaters.
These three kinds of idolatry were signified by the three sons of Terah.
Terah was a son of Nahor, and also a nation named from him... AC 1362.

These are the nativities of Terah () = the origins and derivations of the idolatry from which came the representative Church... Here a third Church after the Flood is treated of, which followed when the second became idolatrous in Terah. Terah, Abram, Nahor, and Haran were idolaters; and also the nations from them...
Terah was a nation from this: that the nations springing from his sons acknowledged him as their father. Explained.
Under Haran (the man), see this reference.

Terah and Abram worshipped other gods, and had no knowledge of Jehovah, nor therefore of what the good and truth of faith are. They had thus become better fitted to receive the seed of Truth than others in Syria. AC 1992:2.
Idolatrous worship in general is signified by Terah.

Terah took Abram his son; and Lot the son of Aaron... and Sarai... and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan () = that they who were in idolatrous worship were instructed in the celestial and spiritual things of faith, in order that a representative Church might thence come forth.

And the days of Terah were 205 years; and Terah died in Haran () = the duration and state of that idolatrous worship; the end of that idolatry; and the beginning of a representative Church through Abram.

Terah, who was the father of three sons: Abram, Nahor, and Haran, represents the common stock from which the Churches were. Terah himself was indeed an idolater; but representatives do not regard the person... And, as the representative Jewish Church commenced in Abraham... therefore Terah and his three sons took on the representation of Churches... AC 4207.
The family of Terah... acknowledged Shaddai as their god.
